Input Field
layers: A form control that accepts a single line of text. Use for short inputs like names, emails, phone numbers, or search fields. Sizes: Small for compact/dense UI, Medium for standard forms, Large for prominent hero-style inputs. Pick the state that matches the interaction the design calls for.

frames.name: Text Area
layers: A form control for editing multi-line text. Use for longer content such as comments, descriptions, feedback, or messages. Sizes: Small for compact panels, Medium for standard forms, Large for content-heavy forms where more visible lines help the user.

frames.name: Single Select Dropdown
layers: A single-select input that lets users choose one option from a list. Also known as a Select menu. Use when there are more options than can comfortably fit as visible radio buttons. Sizes: Small for compact toolbars/filters, Medium for standard forms, Large for prominent form fields. Note: this component has 6 documented states — Focused, Success, and Read Only are not part of its state set.

frames.name: Multi-Select Dropdown
layers: A multi-select input that lets users choose several options from a list, shown as removable tags. Also known as a Select menu (multi-select variant). Use when a user may need to pick more than one option at once. Sizes and states are identical to the single-select Dropdown — the only difference is the Filled state, which renders selected options as tags with an overflow count (e.g. "+2") instead of plain text. This set shares all other state/size specs 1:1 with Dropdown, including its Left Icon, Right Icon, Change Label, Show Hint Message, and Show Left Icon properties.

frames.name: Switch
layers: A control for toggling a single setting on or off immediately (no separate save/submit step). Use inside forms for binary preferences (e.g. "Enable notifications"), not for selecting among multiple options — use Radio Button or Checkbox for that. Migrated from the design system's existing Switch component — states and sizing are unchanged from the source.

frames.name: Radio Button
layers: A control for selecting exactly one option from a set of mutually exclusive choices, where all options should stay visible at once. Use Checkbox instead when the user can select more than one item, or Dropdown when there isn't room to show every option. Migrated from the design system's existing Radio Button component — states and sizing are unchanged from the source.

frames.name: Checkbox
layers: A control for selecting one or more items from a list, or for a single on/off agreement (e.g. terms & conditions). "Uncheck All" is the indeterminate/partial-selection state — use it for a parent checkbox when only some of its children are checked. Migrated from the design system's existing Checkbox component — states and sizing (including the extra XS size) are unchanged from the source.

frames.name: Search Field
layers: A specialized Input Field for filtering or finding content, with a persistent search icon and a clear (×) button once a query is entered. Use this instead of Input Field whenever the control's sole purpose is searching/filtering — use Input Field for general text entry. Shares Input Field's padding, radius, max-height, and color/font tokens exactly. States are intentionally reduced (no Error/Success/Read Only) since search rarely needs form validation.

frames.name: Date Picker Field
layers: A field for selecting a single date, opening a calendar overlay on interaction. Shares Input Field's box, padding, radius, and token scale — the only structural difference is a fixed (non-swappable in practice) calendar icon in place of a generic left icon. The calendar overlay itself is documented separately as the "Calendar" component (see its own frame on this page) — built from a reusable Calendar Day cell assembled into a month grid.

frames.name: Slider
layers: A control for selecting a numeric value (or range of values) by dragging a thumb along a track. Use for approximate/continuous values (volume, brightness, price range) where a precise typed number isn't necessary — pair with Number Input when exact values matter. Track fill and thumb use the same accent blue as Switch's Checked state, so both stay visually consistent as "on/active" signals. The thumb enlarges slightly in the Active (dragging) state for better touch feedback.

frames.name: Phone Number Input
layers: A specialized text field for entering a phone number, prefixed with a tappable country-code segment (flag + dial code + chevron) that opens a country picker on its own. Shares Input Field's padding, radius, and token scale for the number segment. Implementation note: the country-code segment and the number field are two separate interactive targets — clicking the code area should not focus the number input, and vice versa.

frames.name: Autocomplete
layers: A text field that filters a suggestion list as the user types, then commits a value on selection — a hybrid of Input Field and Dropdown. Use when the option list is too long to browse comfortably but the user still benefits from typing to narrow it down. Shares Input Field/Dropdown's box, padding, radius, and token scale. See the "Autocomplete Suggestion" and open-state example below for the panel that appears while typing.

frames.name: Tags Input (Freeform)
layers: A text field where the user types and presses Enter/comma to create their own tags, rather than picking from a fixed list — use this instead of Multi-Select Dropdown when the valid values aren't a closed set (e.g. skills, keywords). Shares Multi-Select Dropdown's tag chip styling exactly. Focused shows an active text cursor after existing tags; Filled shows tags with no active cursor (blurred, nothing being typed). Both are functionally "has tags" states — the difference is only whether the field currently has focus.

frames.name: Number Input / Stepper
layers: A numeric field with increment/decrement buttons flanking a value display. Use for small, bounded quantities (e.g. cart quantity, guest count) where typing isn't as fast as tapping + or −. Shares the field family's padding, radius, and token scale. Implementation note: the value should still accept direct keyboard entry, not just +/− taps — clamp to any min/max on blur, not on every keystroke.

frames.name: File Upload
layers: A dropzone for uploading one or more files via drag-and-drop or a click-to-browse fallback. "Drag Active" is the state shown while a file is being dragged over the zone (not a persistent hover). Once a file is added, replace the dropzone content with a file-row list (name, size, progress bar, remove button) — that list view isn't built yet. The center icon is an instance-swap slot so it can be replaced with a more specific upload/document icon; it defaults to Search only as a placeholder in this file.

frames.name: KPIs & Widgets — Developer Handoff Guide
layers: Built on the KPIs & Widgetets page (node 17:4689), matching the structure and Barlow/#101828/#475467 visual language of the existing Buttons, Forms, Tables, Header, and Side Bar Developer Handoff Guides in this file.

This library exists so that any KPIs & Widgets page — a fixed dashboard, a drag-and-drop custom dashboard, or a new page an AI agent is assembling — can be built entirely by mixing and matching existing components at the right size for the space available, without ever needing a bespoke one-off card. Every card ships in multiple "Grid Size" variants for exactly this reason.
Always start from an existing KPI component in this library — never draw a card from scratch. The library lives in the "KPIs and widgets Library refence" section on this page.
• For a fixed dashboard layout: duplicate the closest matching reference screen and swap components/content.
• For a drag-and-drop custom dashboard: drag a KPI type onto the canvas, then resize the instance to the target slot — see Section 4.

Verified directly against this file's actual components: 7 card types plus "KPIs Line Charts" (a graph-driven card with no text overrides), found in the "KPIs and widgets Library refence" and "KPIs Depenedncies" sections on this page.

This is the core rule of the whole library: no KPI card has a single fixed width. "Grid Size" tells you which layout/density a variant was designed for — the actual instance is then stretched by auto-layout to exactly fill whatever slot it lands in on the real page. Confirmed by real production references (Sand file): the same power-metric card renders at different widths depending on how many cards share its row.
Two different gutters — don't mix them up
Anatomy to preserve on every card, at every size
These stay constant regardless of Grid Size — only the internal content density and the outer width change.
Real mix-and-match combinations seen in production (Sand file)

Four small "atom" components are instanced inside the cards above (found in the "KPIs Depenedncies" section). Fix these once and every card using them updates automatically — never override them locally inside a card instance.
6. AI Agent Guide — Assembling KPI Pages & Custom Dashboards
Applies whenever an agent is building a KPIs & Widgets page, a fixed dashboard, or dragging KPIs into a user's custom dashboard canvas.
1. Only use the KPI types already in this library (Section 3). Never invent a visually new KPI card type on your own initiative.

2. For each slot to fill, pick the KPI type that matches the metric, then pick the Grid Size variant whose density best matches the slot's available width — not necessarily its exact pixel width (Section 4).
3. Let auto-layout FILL sizing stretch the instance to the slot's exact width. Never hand-set a one-off width that fights the library's sizing.
4. Use the 12px KPI-to-KPI gutter within a row/column and the 24px page margin at the outer edge — never swap the two (Section 4).

5. If the data you need to show does not match any existing KPI type: STOP. Ask the requester directly: "No existing KPI type covers [metric]. Should I (a) flag this for the designer to add manually, or (b) do you want me to design and build it now?"

6. If given the green light to build a new type yourself, it MUST keep the established anatomy: 16px padding, 16px corner radius, 1px stroke, Surface/Light/White background, and fonts/colors/spacing bound to the same tokens as every other card.
